item.title: JPMorgan, Santander Lead £1.1 Billion Loan for Drax Solar Deal
item.description: Banks including JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Banco Santander SA are leading a debt financing of more than £1 billion to fund Drax Group Plc’s purchase of renewable energy company Bluefield Solar Income Fund.
item.dc:creator: Eleanor Duncan and Claire Ruckin

item.title: Three Dead in Another School Shooting in Southern Philippines
item.description: Three people died while eight were injured in a school shooting in southern Philippines on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Neil Jerome Morales

item.title: There's a Mind-Boggling Number of Rich People in America
item.description: In 2014, the economists Owen Zidar and Eric Zwick were asked by the Treasury to conduct a study on the tax burden of private business owners. It was tricky to figure out how much these sorts of business owners — auto dealers, contractors, the like — actually owed in taxes: After Reagan's 1986 tax reforms, pass-through businesses and other accounting tricks became widespread enough to obscure this class of wealthy Americans hiding in plain sight. The research they conducted led to their new book The Everywhere Millionaire: Who Is Really Rich in America and How They Got There, and one of their central findings is that there are about three million private business owners who have an average wealth of around $25 million. They call this group “Main Street Millionaires” and their influence on the economy and politics in the US is considerable. We speak with Zidar and Zwick about how they measured the actual number of rich people in America. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What Is the Treasury Bonds Basis Trade, and Is It Over?
item.description: Global bond markets have been roiled since the Iran-US conflict began. Surging energy prices together with massive corporate borrowing and ever-expanding government debt issuance have sent Treasury bond prices plummeting, pushing yields to the highest level in nearly two decades. The rout prompted US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in August to increase buybacks of the government’s own longer-dated bonds, in an unusual intervention aimed at lowering Americans’ borrowing costs.
item.dc:creator: Ye Xie and Cameron Fozi

item.title: Prudential Exits AlexForbes as Motsepe’s ARC Boosts Stake
item.description: A firm linked to billionaire Patrice Motsepe is consolidating control of Alexander Forbes Group Holdings Ltd. through a deal that will see US financial-services giant Prudential Financial Inc. exit its investment in South Africa’s biggest standalone retirement-fund administrator.
item.dc:creator: Adelaide Changole

item.title: ECB's Kazaks Says Restrictive Policy May Be Appropriate
item.description: European Central Bank Governing Council member and Bank of Latvia Governor Martins Kazaks discusses the second-round inflation effects of the energy price shock and the outlook for interest rates. "With the economy forecasted to close the output gap next year, you know, wading into restrictive territory, in my view, would be appropriate," Kazaks tells Bloomberg's Oliver Crook in Dublin. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Pushes, BOJ Splinters Over Rate Hike
item.description: Insight with Haslinda Amin, a daily news program featuring in-depth, high-profile interviews and analysis to give viewers the complete picture on the stories that matter. The show features prominent leaders spanning the worlds of business, finance, politics and culture. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: PSA Is Said to Consider Selling Stake in Mumbai Port Operations
item.description: PSA International is considering selling a minority stake in its container terminal operations in Jawaharlal Nehru Port in Mumbai, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Baiju Kalesh, Elffie Chew and P R Sanjai

item.title: Uzbek Logistics Firm Centrum Taps Citi, JPMorgan for London IPO
item.description: Uzbekistan’s largest private logistics group is in talks with Citigroup Inc. and JPMorgan Chase & Co. to work on its initial public offering in London, according to people familiar with the situation.
item.dc:creator: Yuliya Fedorinova, Laura Gardner Cuesta and Nariman Gizitdinov

item.title: Sea Clash Shows China Pushing Closer to Philippine Mainland
item.description: China and the Philippines traded accusations after their vessels collided in the South China Sea on Friday in one of the closest such confrontations to the Philippine mainland.
item.dc:creator: Cliff Venzon and Andreo Calonzo

item.title: Turkey Turns to Two Big Banks to Liquidate Troubled Funds
item.description: Turkey has turned to two of its biggest banks to oversee the liquidation of 131 investment funds caught up in turmoil that has shaken the country’s asset-management industry.
item.dc:creator: Inci Ozbek and Tugce Ozsoy

item.title: Indonesia’s Finance Chief Keeps $17 Billion With State Banks
item.description: Indonesia’s new finance minister will retain the policy of his predecessor of keeping about $17 billion in the government’s standby funds with state lenders to help boost borrowing and economic activity.
item.dc:creator: Grace Sihombing

item.title: Strategists Say Ueda’s Less-Hawkish Comments Weighed on Yen
item.description: The yen extended losses as Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda’s comments at a press conference disappointed investors who were looking for a more hawkish tone, strategists said. The BOJ needed to avoid letting prices deviate above target and harming the economy, Ueda said, speaking after the central bank raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point to 1.25% in a split vote.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Burgess, Eru Ishikawa and John Cheng

item.title: Yen Extends Declines After Ueda Gives Mixed Signals on Hikes
item.description: The yen extended its drop against the dollar after Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda gave mixed signals about future rate hikes.
item.dc:creator: John Cheng

item.title: Gold Extends Gain as Lower Oil, Fed Hike Temper Inflation Fears
item.description: Gold extended a gain at the end of a volatile week as the Federal Reserve’s first interest-rate hike since 2023 and lower oil prices helped ease concerns about inflation.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie

item.title: Block Thames Creditors From Taking Control, UK Lawmakers Say
item.description: Thames Water’s senior creditors should be blocked from taking full control over the utility, a group of British lawmakers said Friday.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Shankleman

item.title: Stocks Rise as Tech Rallies and Oil Prices Retreat: Markets Wrap
item.description: Technology stocks drove equity gains in the US and Asia as lower oil prices buoyed broader sentiment, setting markets up for an upbeat end to a turbulent week.
item.dc:creator: Andre Janse van Vuuren and Macarena Muñoz

item.title: Airtel Money Is Said to Trim IPO Size Ahead of Deal Kick Off
item.description: Airtel Money’s owners are considering raising less money than previously sought in the company’s initial public offering, a listing process that could start as soon as next week, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Mayo Cerqueiro, Vinicy Chan, Loni Prinsloo and Swetha Gopinath
